headline: Corn and beans break lower; crude tops $101 on tight supply
lead: Corn settled Friday at $4.74¼, down 3¾ cents, and beans closed at $12.61¼, off 1¾ cents, both pressured by harvest supply all week. Crude gained 3.5% to $101.41 after the IEA pushed emergency stock releases and the US offered another 17 million barrels from the reserve.
teaser: Corn and beans eased again on harvest supply while crude topped $101 on a tightening fuel market.

one_number.unit: Equatorial Guinea oil output drop since 2020
one_number.context: OPEC's smallest producer fell to 20,000 barrels a day from 140,000, a small but real piece of the tight global supply pushing crude higher.

sections.title: Corn and beans ease into the weekend
sections.body:
- Corn settled at **$4.74¼**, down 3¾ cents, the third straight lower close as harvest supply keeps weighing on the board.
- Beans held closer to flat at $12.61¼, down just 1¾ cents, with China back in the market booking its first cargoes since the Trump-Xi summit.
sections.so_what: Chinese demand is steadying beans while corn and wheat take the harvest pressure alone.

sections.title: Cattle firm on cash hopes
sections.body:
- Live cattle closed at **$227.55**, up 0.7%, and feeders held near flat at $343.625.
- Packing plant closures are tightening where feeders can be sold, with some finishers now hauling cattle farther to find a bid.
- Hogs added half a percent to $66.925, a quiet close after a quiet week.
sections.so_what: Cash hopes are lifting cattle even as some feeders face fewer places to sell.

sections.title: Crude tops $101 on tight supply
sections.body:
- WTI crude traded at **$101.41**, up 3.5%, after the IEA accelerated emergency releases and the US offered another 17 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
- Equatorial Guinea's output has broke down 85% since 2020, a small cut that still tightens the global barrel count.
sections.so_what: Diesel costs for fall fieldwork are the number to watch, not the barrel price alone.

outside_the_pit.title: Winter weather outlook webinar set for Wednesday, Oct 21
outside_the_pit.body: A livestream on what a strong El Niño pattern means for winter temperatures and precipitation runs Wednesday at 1 p.m. CT.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress report; watch harvest pace against the five-year average as basis sits at seasonal lows.
Corn back above $4.80 would say harvest pressure is easing; a close under $4.70 says it is not.
Export sales; another confirmed China soybean buy would help beans hold $12.60.

source_summary: CME settlement data, USDA, feedstuffs.com, agweb.com, farmdocdaily.illinois.edu, farmpolicynews.illinois.edu, beefmagazine.com, thefencepost.com, oilprice.com, drovers.com

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.91 vs $4.62 projected (+6.3%), 12 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.83 vs $11.09 projected (+15.7%), 12 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Ours: the average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 16, figured the way USDA RMA does. RMA posts corn at $4.92 and soybeans at $12.85, both through Oct 15. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 16. Oct 1-31 window, most states.

facts.sentence: On Friday, Oct 16, 1,494 of the 1,527 elevators AGSIST reads posted a lower cash corn bid than Thursday, 25 a higher one; 132 changed their basis, 57 weaker and 75 stronger.
facts.detail: 8 unchanged; median change 5¢ lower. Biggest state move: Iowa, 5¢ lower (306 elevators). 3 outliers left out.
facts.unit: cents per bushel, median change in cash bid
facts.source: AGSIST elevator network, last posted bid per trading day (data/bids-prev)

facts.sentence: On Friday, Oct 16, 1,270 of the 1,328 elevators AGSIST reads posted a lower cash soybean bid than Thursday, 49 a higher one; 174 changed their basis, 114 weaker and 60 stronger.
facts.detail: 9 unchanged; median change 2¢ lower. Biggest state move: Iowa, 2¢ lower (269 elevators).
facts.unit: cents per bushel, median change in cash bid

facts.sentence: Corn basis on Oct 17 ran from 55¢ over December futures in Texas to 80¢ under in North Dakota and South Dakota, state medians of the elevators AGSIST reads.
facts.detail: Elevators behind each median: Texas 17, North Dakota 37, South Dakota 89. 15 states with 15 or more.
facts.unit: cents per bushel between the strongest and weakest state median
